name: InStride Health
one_liner: Virtual exposure-based therapy (CBT/ERP) and psychiatry for children, teens and young adults ages 7 to 26 with anxiety or OCD.
best_for: Children and teens with moderate to severe anxiety or OCD who need more than weekly therapy
Families who want exposure-based CBT plus medication management from one team
Families with in-network insurance in the states it serves
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
Young people who need inpatient or residential care
short_description: Virtual specialty anxiety and OCD care for ages 7–26 from a three-person team, mostly covered by in-network insurance in about ten states and DC.
long_description: InStride Health, launched in 2022 with support from McLean Hospital, provides outpatient virtual treatment for children, teens and young adults (ages 7 to 26) with moderate to severe anxiety, OCD and related problems. Care uses cognitive behavioral therapy with exposure and response prevention, delivered by a coordinated team of a therapist, an exposure coach and a psychiatric clinician, and includes caregivers. Programmes usually last 4 to 8 months and most families start within 1 to 4 weeks. It is in-network with plans including Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Optum and UnitedHealthcare and serves CT, MA, ME, NH, NJ, NY, OH, PA, RI, VA and DC; the young person must be in a served state during sessions. Its outcome reports are company-run; one peer-reviewed, company-authored cohort study (2026) reported less caregiver strain after treatment.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; self-pay price given by phone
pricing.notes: In-network with plans including Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Optum and UnitedHealthcare (varies by state). A self-pay option exists for families without in-network coverage; call 855-438-8331 for the price. Programmes usually run 4 to 8 months.

privacy.notes: Says it does not sell personal information for financial gain, but describes interest-based advertising cookies and a California opt-out of 'sales'; treatment records fall under its HIPAA notice, which says PHI is not sold or used for marketing.

clinical_trials.outcome: Caregiver strain (CGSQ-SF7) fell from admission to discharge; no control group; both authors are InStride employees.

primary_uses: Exposure and response prevention (ERP) for OCD
CBT with exposure for anxiety disorders
Caregiver coaching for anxiety and OCD

patient_summary: You apply online or call, and if your child fits, a three-person team (therapist, exposure coach and psychiatric clinician) runs video sessions over about 4 to 8 months, with more practice between sessions than standard weekly therapy. Most families pay through in-network insurance such as Aetna, BCBS, Optum or UnitedHealthcare; self-pay is available but the price is given by phone.

availability.note: Ages 7–26. Serves CT, MA, ME, NH, NJ, NY, OH, PA, RI, VA and DC; the patient must be in a served state during sessions.
